look_here_first: TEXAS FESCUE — FIRST check a rooted, persistent PERENNIAL tuft in wooded habitat, with a loose 8–30 cm panicle whose flexible branches droop and carry separate 6–9 mm spikelets (usually 2–4 fertile florets). Then use a hand lens: true hairless-edged MEMBRANOUS ligule 0.5–1 mm; lower glume 4–7 mm and 1-veined, upper 5.5–7 mm and 3-veined; fertile lemma 5–7 mm, 5-veined, AWNLESS or only minutely pointed. Do not confuse the historical F. johnsonii drawing with a modern verified living photo. Current archived photograph is loose fragments and does not independently prove this identification. Compare tiny annual awned F. octoflora, and check other woodland fescues by glume/lemma and rooted crown.

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.growth_form: Perennial tufted grass; culms 50–100 cm; leaf blades flat or folded, 2–5 mm wide; sheath surfaces glabrous.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.panicle: Open, flexuous, 8–30 cm; primary branches drooping; spikelets clustered toward branch tips.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.spikelet: 6–9 mm, laterally compressed, 2–4 fertile florets; uppermost reduced; glumes persist after florets separate.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.fertile_lemma: 5–7 mm, obscurely 5-veined, tip acute/acuminate, awnless or minutely mucronate; do not mistake a tiny mucro for a long awn.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.ligule_collar: True eciliate (without hair fringe) membrane 0.5–1 mm; photograph junction with 1-mm scale. No species-specific auricle claim without an attached specimen.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.evidence_note: All measurements are published taxon-level ranges, not verified on the existing loose-fragment photograph.

crew_lookalike_key_20261023: Festuca octoflora (sixweeks fescue): shallow-rooted cool-season ANNUAL; often narrower contracted panicle, 5–17 florets, fertile lemma ending in a true awn (0.3–6 mm in Kew GrassBase). Do not identify by panicle silhouette alone.

Festuca subverticillata / F. nutans (nodding fescue complex): also woodland, spreading/drooping panicles and awnless florets. Distinguish with verified current taxon determination, glume and lemma measurements, mature floret count and attached crown; do not transfer its dimensions to F. versuta.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · AWNLESS LEMMA
field_id_short_tiles.short: 5–7 mm, five veins; tiny point possible
field_id_short_tiles.details: Fertile lemma 5–7 mm, obscurely 5-veined, with an acute or acuminate apex, AWNLESS or merely minutely mucronate. A tiny terminal point is not the long projecting awn seen on sixweeks fescue. The 2-veined palea lies within the floret. No present photograph measures these structures.
field_id_short_tiles.status: WHOLE SPIKELET PHOTO HELPFUL; LEMMA NERVES AND MUCRO NOT MEASURED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · OPEN THE COLLAR
field_id_short_tiles.details: Expose the inner blade–sheath junction of the same identified plant. The true ligule is a short eciliate (hairless-edged) membrane 0.5–1 mm; leaf blades are generally flat or folded, 2–5 mm wide. Do not infer the ligule from loose spikelets or a sheath edge.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · SPLIT THE FESCUES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Texas perennial and awnless; sixweeks annual and awned
field_id_short_tiles.details: Sixweeks fescue (F. octoflora = Vulpia octoflora) has an annual fibrous base, narrow often crowded panicle, 5–17 florets and an awn on its lemma. Texas fescue has a persistent crown, loose drooping head, 2–4 florets and no long awn. Other woodland fescues can overlap: hold species confirmation without source-vouchered crown and dissected spikelet. Preserve the unresolved Hays occurrence.
